rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Great meeting you too. We'll put together a focused two-pager and budget — likely scoped around building a small, checkable evaluation suite for a currently under-measured risk (how well agentic AI systems resist instructions smuggled into the content they process, e.g. emails or web pages trying to get an agent to take unauthorized actions). We'll have it to you before the 30th. One quick question as we scope the budget: does the rapid round fund API/inference costs for running an eval against multiple models, or is it meant more for researcher time? Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Idris at Emberfall: told him we're preparing a proposal around that project, due before Nov 30.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — genuinely useful timing. The thing I'm circling as a first concrete project: a small test suite for whether agentic AI systems resist \"prompt injection\" — instructions hidden in emails, web pages, or files they process that try to get them to take unauthorized actions (send money, leak data, etc.). It's narrow, measurable, and under-covered. If you're up for it, the most useful five-hours-a-week things right now would be: (1) helping design a clean taxonomy of injection scenarios and a scoring rubric, and/or (2) running a small batch of tests against a couple of agent setups and analyzing the results. No funding in place yet to pay for this — it'd be volunteer for now, and I'll say so plainly before you commit any time. Want to do a short call this week to see if it's a fit? Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman (the volunteer from the meetup): proposed she help design the eval scenarios / run and analyze tests, made clear it's unpaid for now, suggested a call.
